title: Finite Element Analysis Model for Assessing Expansion Patterns from Surgically Assisted Rapid Palatal Expansion
protocol: Acquire a human CBCT image of the head in a natural head position that includes the patient's maxillary complex, including the maxillary basal bone, maxillary alveolar bone, and maxillary dentition.
Import the CBCT DICOM files into Mimics software.
Create New Project (Ctrl + N), select all the DICOM images, and click Next and Convert.
Define the direction of the model (A: anterior, P: posterior, T: top, B: bottom, L: left, R: right) and click OK.
Segment the file into maxillary complex, maxillary first premolars, and maxillary first molars.
Click Thresholding, select an appropriate threshold to segment bones, and click Apply.
Create new masks and click Edit Masks, using Draw and Erase to segment the patient's maxillary complex, maxillary first premolars, and maxillary first molars.
Export the targets as stereolithography (STL) files.
Right-click on masks and select Calculate 3D to generate 3D objects.
Right-click on 3D objects, select STL+, choose the demanded objects, and press Add and Finish to create STL files.
Import STL files into Geomagic software.
Click File > Open, select the STL files, then press Open.
Choose Millimeters for the data in Units pop-up window and click OK.
Smooth the surface of the maxillary complex using Polygons > Remove Spikes.
Drag the smoothness level near Low, click Apply, and OK.
Smooth the surface further by clicking Polygons > Relax Polygons.
Drag the smoothness level near Min, click Apply, and OK.
Repair intersections by clicking Polygons > Repair Intersections.
Choose Relax/Clean in the Mode window, click Apply, and OK.
Modify the surface into a continuous region by dragging sharp surfaces and pressing delete to create holes.
Fill up the holes using Polygons > Fill Holes.
Use Fill, Fill Partial, Create Bridges in the Fill Method window.
Click Apply, and OK.
Convert 2D surface to a 3D solid model.
Click Edit > Phase > Shape Phase, select Edit contours to sketch the surface, then click OK.
Draw quadrilateral meshes using Draw Patch Layout to cover all surfaces, then click OK.
Define a proper Resolution in Construct Grids and click OK to generate finer mesh.
Construct 3D solid model by clicking Fit Surfaces, click Apply, and OK.
Export the 3D model as an IGES file named Maxilla.
Create the cancellous bone by reducing the volume of the maxillary complex by 1 mm from the buccal alveolar surface.
Create periodontal ligament space by expanding the contour of the roots by 0.2 mm.
Click Polygon Phase, choose Delete in the Contour Lines window, select Preserve in the Patch Layout window, then press OK to convert the 3D solid model into a 2D surface.
Click Polygons > Offset, enter -1 mm and 0.2 mm in the Distance panel for cancellous bone and periodontal ligament, then click Apply and OK.
Click Edit > Phase > Shape Phase, select Restore Patch Layout and press OK.
Click Construct Grids, define a proper Resolution, and click OK to generate a finer mesh.
Click Fit Surfaces, click Apply, and OK to construct a 3D solid model.
Click File > Save as to export the 3D model and save it in IGES files (named CB and PL).
Import the CAD files into SolidWorks.
Click File > Open, select the Maxilla file, and press Open to import the CAD file.
Click File > Save to save the file into the Part format.
Construct the cancellous bone below the palatal plane (PP).
Click Insert > Part, select the CB file, and press Open to import the CAD file.
Click Insert > Reference Geometry > Plane, choose three feature points on the palatal plane, and click OK to create a cutting plane.
Click Insert > Features > Split, choose the palatal plane in Trim Tools, and click Cut Part to create a cutting preview.
Tick the checkboxes in the Resulting Bodies, and click OK to separate the cancellous bone.
Click the cancellous bone above the palatal plane, right-click, and press Delete in the Body section.
Construct the periodontal ligament of maxillary first premolars and maxillary first molars.
Click Insert > Part, select the PL file, and press Open to import the CAD file.
Click Insert > Features > Intersect, and choose Maxilla and PL in the Selections window.
Select Create both in the Selections window, choose the periodontal ligament part in the Region List, then click OK to generate the ligament.
Perform a midpalatal cutting plane from the anterior nasal spine (ANS) to posterior nasal spine (PNS) and retain the right half of the maxillary complex.
Click Insert > Reference Geometry > Plane, choose three feature points on the midpalatal plane, and click OK to create a cutting plane.
Click Insert > Features > Split, choose the palatal plane in Trim Tools, and click Cut Part to create a cutting preview.
Tick the checkboxes in the Resulting Bodies, and click OK to separate the maxillary complex.
Click the left half of the maxillary complex, right-click, and press Delete in the Body section.
Mirror the right half of the maxillary complex and create an identical left half.
Click Insert > Pattern/Mirror > Mirror, and choose the midpalatal plane in Mirror Face/Plane.
Choose all the right half maxillary complex in Bodies to Mirror, and click OK to generate the left half of the maxillary complex.
Click Insert > Part, select the PL file, and press Open to import the CAD file.
Click Insert > Features > Split, choose the teeth in the PL file, and set a Uniform Scaling of 1.05.
Click OK to generate bands with 0.5 mm in thickness.
Click Insert > Reference Geometry > Plane, choose three feature points on the occlusal plane, and click OK to create a reference plane.
Click Insert > Reference Geometry > Plane, choose the occlusal plane, and set an offset distance of 1.5 mm.
Click OK to create the first cutting plane.
Click Insert > Reference Geometry > Plane, choose the occlusal plane, and set an offset distance of 4.0 mm.
Click OK to create the second cutting plane.
Click Insert > Features > Split, and choose the first and second plane in Trim Tools and the teeth in Target Bodies.
Click Cut Bodies to create a cutting preview.
Tick the checkboxes in the Resulting Bodies, and click OK to separate the teeth.
Click the band above the first plane and below the second plane, right-click, and press Delete in the Body section.
Click Insert > Reference Geometry > Plane, choose three feature points on the hard palate plane, and click OK to create a sketch plane.
Click Insert > Sketch, draw an acrylic plate referring to the Haas expander, and click Exit Sketch.
Click Insert > Boss/Base > Extrude, choose the sketch of the acrylic plate, set 5 mm in Depth, and click OK.
Click Insert > Features > Flex, and bend the acrylic plate to fit the anatomy of the palate.
Click Insert > Features > Fillet/Round, and fillet the sharp edges of the acrylic plate with a radius of 1 mm.
Click Insert > Reference Geometry > Plane, choose three feature points on the band, and click OK to create a sketch plane (named P1).
Click Insert > Sketch, draw a circle 2 mm in diameter, and click Exit Sketch (named C1).
Click Insert > Reference Geometry > Plane, choose three feature points on the acrylic plate, and click OK to create a sketch plane (named P2).
Click Insert > Sketch, draw a circle 2 mm in diameter, and click Exit Sketch (named C2).
Click Insert > Reference Geometry > Plane, choose the P2 plane, set an offset distance of 6 mm, and click OK.
Click Insert > Sketch, draw a circle 2 mm in diameter, and click Exit Sketch (named C3).

Click Insert > Boss/Base > Loft, choose the C1, C2, and C3 sketches in Profiles window, select the band and the acrylic plate in Feature Scope window, tick Merge Result in Options window, and click OK.
Create a 1 mm thick plane from the corner of the piriform aperture towards the infra zygomatic crest at various degrees from the horizontal plane.
Click Insert > Reference Geometry > Plane, choose three feature points on the osteotomy plane and click OK to create the plane (named O1).
Click Insert > Reference Geometry > Plane, choose the osteotomy plane, set an offset distance of 1.0 mm, and click OK to create an inferior cutting plane (named O2).
Click Insert > Features > Split, choose the O1 and O2 planes in Trim Tools, and click Cut Part to create a cutting preview.
Tick the checkboxes in the Resulting Bodies, and click OK to separate the maxillary complex.
Click the body between O1 and O2 planes, right-click, and press Delete in the Body section.
Export models with different buccal osteotomy angles in Parasolid Model Part File (X_T) for analysis.
Click File > Save as, choose Parasolid (x_t) in the File Type list, and click Save to export the models.
Click and drag the Static Structural from Toolbox to create an analysis workspace.
Double-click Engineering Data, and set Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio of all materials in Properties.
Import the maxillary complex model by clicking Geometry, then File > Import External Geometry File, and click Generate.
Generate the cortical bone and periodontal ligament by Boolean with cancellous bone and teeth using Create > Boolean.
Double-click Model, and click Geometry to select material properties for each part.
Right-click Mesh and click Generate Mesh to build elements on the model.
Assign soft/small parts in Contact Bodies and stiff/large parts in Target Bodies under Connections.
Assign contact type and friction coefficient in Definition.
Insert a Spring connection right-clicking Connections to connect upper and lower parts of the osteotomy plane.
Set springs as 1 mm long with spring constant k = 60 N/mm, placing one at each grid node.
Apply a clinically acceptable force along the x-axis on the acrylic plate for various combinations of osteotomies.
Right-click Static Structural, click Insert > Fixed Support and set the structure on the palatal plane immovable.
Right-click Static Structural and insert a force of 150 N directed away from the medial line on the acrylic plate.
Insert Total Deformation under Solution to monitor expansion deformation.
Conduct a convergence test until expansions on both sides are achieved.
Click Solve to initiate the simulation and wait for the Force Convergence level to meet the criterion.
Display the expansion results using Total Deformation.

Measure displacements of specified anatomic landmarks in three dimensions: mesioincisal line angle of maxillary central incisor (U1), buccal cusp tip of maxillary first premolar (U4), mesiobuccal cusp tip of maxillary first molar (U6), lateroinferior corner of the piriform aperture (Alar), infra-zygomatic crest (IZC), and midpoint of the expander.
